semantically_equivalent_models.justification: "Model-free agent" typically refers to agents that learn from interaction with an environment in reinforcement learning, without explicitly using a model of the environment. Thus, a 'reinforcement learning agent' being a broader category, can be semantically equivalent.

RL (reinforcement learning) agents include both model-free and model-based agents. Given the context, an 'rl agent' is semantically equivalent to a model-free agent as it represents the broader category.

parent_models.justification: An 'agent-based model' is a broader category that encompasses various types of agents, including model-free agents.
A 'deep reinforcement learning model' can encompass both model-free and model-based approaches, making it a parent model for a model-free agent.
This is a very broad category that would include all forms of reinforcement learning agents, including model-free agents, as part of artificial intelligence.

closest_parent_model.justification: The term 'agent-based model' is specifically about models composed of interacting agents, similar to model-free agents that work independently within a larger framework.

child_models.justification: Multi-agent PPO represents a more specific application or variation of model-free approaches in reinforcement learning in collaborative settings.
These refer to agents that incorporate recurrence in their learning process, adding another layer of complexity and specificity to the basic model-free agent.

closest_child_model.justification: 'Multi-agent PPO' specifically denotes a policy gradient method within reinforcement learning, which is a subset of model-free deep reinforcement learning techniques, making it closely related.

sibling_models.justification: 'Individual-based models' are similar in the sense they focus on individual units (agents) interacting within a system, much like model-free agents.
'pr agent' suggests a similar structure to model-free agents as it seems to refer to decision-making agents in environments.

closest_sibling_model.justification: 'Individual-based models' involve modeling individual entities within a system, aligning closely with the idea of model-free agents as autonomous units within a larger model.
